name: Jakim
overview: Jakim was a male Levite who served as the twelfth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in Israel. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the sons of Aaron, which is noted in the division of priestly duties. His role as a priest placed him within the sacred service of God as part of the Levitical tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Jakim means 'he will establish,' reflecting a meaning rooted in stability or foundation. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a significant Hebrew meaning that may reflect the role or character attributed to him.
familyAndRelationships: Jakim is identified as a descendant of Ithamar, linking him to one of the two priestly lines descending from Aaron. Scripture does not record additional family relationships beyond this connection within the priestly lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Jakim's importance lies in his inclusion among the twenty-four priestly courses, specifically as the twelfth chosen, which structured the organized service of priests in Israel. His lineage from Ithamar highlights the continuation of priestly duties through Aaron's descendants, emphasizing the orderly distribution of sacred responsibilities. This arrangement ensured the proper worship and service to God as prescribed in Israel's religious system.
